thesis: Status-quo anchor on the Silver Bulletin net approval of -22.3 (16 Oct 2026), near a record low, with a ~4-point SD over 75 days for midterm and other shocks.

Midterm penalty for the president's party, a 5-11 point Democratic generic-ballot lead and a razor-thin starting majority put Democratic control near 90%, matching Kalshi and Polymarket at 90-92%. Most sensitive to a late generic-ballot reversal; Other (a tie) is negligible.

No founding member has ever triggered Article 50, no process is pending, and the window is about 10 weeks. Markets for any EU member leaving price a few percent. The forecast is most sensitive to a government announcing a binding exit vote or a formal notice, and none is visible.

Noem, Bondi and Gabbard have already left (3 certain on a literal reading), and markets imply about 1.6 more exits among the remaining 12 before 2027, with a right tail from a possible post-midterm shakeup.

58% of best-of-seven World Series since 1905 reached a Game 6 (68/117, Baseball-Reference), and 54% did from 2000 to 2025. A game-by-game model using the Brewers' ~61% title odds after removing the bookmaker margin (DraftKings -170) gives ~60%. The forecast is most sensitive to how big Milwaukee's per-game edge over the AL champion really is: a bigger edge makes a sweep or a 4-1 result more likely.

GDPNow sits at 3.6% (Oct 15), and Polymarket and Kalshi put about 65-70% on a print of 3.0% or more, which centres the advance estimate near 3.3% once GDPNow's usual overshoot is allowed for. The tails are wide because the nowcast rests on a large inventory build (+1.9pp) offset by a large net-export drag (-2.7pp), and the Q2 advance print missed its nowcasts by more than 1pp.

Advisory committees side with sponsors about 60% of the time, but less often after an FDA rejection. Here the rejection is efficacy-only, the trial met its primary endpoint with a clean safety profile, clinical consensus is pro-atropine, and the panel was convened through the sponsor's formal dispute, which tilts a benefit-risk vote toward YES. The forecast is most sensitive to how harshly the FDA briefing frames the modest 0.01% effect and the missing axial-length data.

I treat the index as a random walk from the live level of about 5,607 on Oct 19 (Yahoo Finance) over about 8.5 sessions. The spread comes from 2026's extreme volatility, roughly 3.2% a day after the chip sell-off and circuit breaker on Oct 15. The forecast is most sensitive to whether that volatility persists or fades.

A random walk from the ~$61 October 16 close (Yahoo Finance), 9 sessions out, with about 120% annualised volatility and fat tails, because the stock is in a credit-stress episode (2032 bonds near a 15% yield, record CDS). Short-covering and 'overblown' calls roughly offset financing and contagion risk, so the median is not tilted. The forecast is most sensitive to any new financing or distress news before October 29.

Northeast Pacific ACE is 343.1 (Climatlas, Oct 19), and the dying Hurricane Trudy should add only ~3 more units (NHC). That leaves the total near 346, so YES most likely needs the low south of Guatemala (NHC: 90% 7-day formation chance) to become a tropical storm or hurricane worth ~4+ ACE before Oct 29. The forecast is most sensitive to whether 343.1 already includes Trudy's Oct 18 fixes.

Brent is about $107.9 on 19 Oct (Trading Economics), roughly 3.7% above the threshold with 8.5 trading days left. A driftless lognormal at about 50% annualised volatility gives about 65% for a close above $104. I shade that to 62% because this year's de-escalation headlines have repeatedly cut 6-8% in a day. The forecast is most sensitive to whether a US-Iran de-escalation headline lands before 29 Oct.

The W40 FDOH report (Oct 4-10) lists 8 counties, the count is cumulative, and over the past seven weeks it rose by about one county every two weeks. I expect roughly 0-1 more by the W42 report: 8 (40%) or 9 (33%) are most likely. The forecast is most sensitive to any new county announcing a first local case or positive mosquito pool before Oct 24.

As of Oct 19, history.md still lists only the three Oct 7 withdrawals, and no commit has changed a manuscript since Oct 8. OpenAI has preferred revising to withdrawing (14 to 1), so a new fatal flaw would need to be found, judged unfixable and logged within about 10 days. The forecast is most sensitive to whether an outside expert shows a specific result is false before Oct 29.

Core PCE has been 3.0% y/y for three months. Nowcasts that map the hot September CPI and PPI into PCE put September core at 0.32-0.34% m/m and 3.1% y/y (TD Securities, WSJ/Timiraos), clearly above the ~0.2% Sep-2025 m/m that drops out. The main uncertainty is the unrounded August level, which splits the risk toward 3.0 or 3.2.

Weekly counts held at 71-87 in E-weeks 35-40, but the partial E-week 41 daily counts point to about 62-70 as the May-October peak season winds down (NEA). I project a mild further decline for E-week 42's provisional first print, with wide tails. The forecast is most sensitive to the settled E-week 41 total.

The FDOH total was 368 at Week 40, after recent weekly additions of +62, +44 and +72 (mean about 59). Two more weeks at a slightly seasonally damped ~55 per week gives about 480, with a right skew in case the epidemic is still accelerating. The forecast depends most on the Week 41 increment due around Oct 22.

Direct leader contact has run about once every 1–3 weeks, which gives a base rate of about 12–15% for any given 2-day window. I shade that down because nothing is scheduled for 29–30 Oct, Trump is openly hostile after the 10 Oct 'new president' remarks and the diesel and Starlink disputes, the current channel runs through envoys, and it is the last week of the midterm campaign. The number is most sensitive to whether a US-brokered negotiation round lands on those dates.

The 16 Oct NEA snapshot shows 3 clusters with 10 or more cases. These are a new, growing Lentor Gardens cluster plus the long-running Bishan St 12 and Ho Ching Rd clusters, and both of those still add about 2 cases a week. Weekly cases are flat at about 70-90, so persistence dominates. Most mass is on 2-3, with the forecast most sensitive to whether Ho Ching or Bishan stops producing cases before 29 Oct.

The post has been vacant since 16 October (Wikipedia). NBC sources say Trump is unlikely to name a successor soon, and the last search took six weeks. Only about 11 days remain, and an acting deputy does not count. The main risk is a fast internal promotion of Anna Kelly, the Kalshi favourite.

The last close was 648 bp (Rava, 16 Oct), after four days of increases to near the 2026 high of about 655. Historical volatility of about ±50 bp over 9 trading days sets the width. I center slightly below the last close because the index has fallen back from this level before. The Brazilian runoff on 25 October is the main event risk, so both tails are wide.

The last three FDOH weekly reports showed 62, 44 and 72 new local cases, so the outbreak is still at its peak. Intensive spraying and the end of the mosquito season argue for a plateau or slow decline rather than further growth. The forecast is most sensitive to the Week 41 report (due ~Oct 22) and to batching of lab results.

AWS growth has accelerated from 20% to 24%, 28% and then 36.7% over four quarters, and it beat AWS consensus by roughly 2-5 pp in each of the last three. With consensus near 37-38% ($45.1B per HSBC), I expect about 40%, with wide tails. The result depends most on how much new AI capacity came online in Q3.

Recent weekly U.S. wheat net sales for 2026/27 have ranged from about 255,000 to 450,000 MT (319,900 MT in the week to Oct 8, a four-week average near 270,000 MT). Lagging HRW sales and a lower USDA export forecast offset Black Sea disruption that favours U.S. origin. The result is most sensitive to whether a large tender or flash sale lands in the week ending Oct 22, so the right tail is wide.

Day 4 of the 2023 timeline, which matches 2026's, had 103,617 votes in the final table (~90k as reported live, ordinary votes only); 2017 had 73k and COVID-era 2020 had 110k. Closing enrolment before voting opens and a larger pre-voting roll roughly offset each other, so the forecast is anchored near 90-95k. It is most sensitive to whether the 2026 live table shows ordinary votes only or combined votes, and to campaign enthusiasm.

AMZN sits at about $253 (Oct 16 close $250.00, Oct 19 pre-market $255) with 9 sessions plus an earnings print priced at ±7.6% by options. That is roughly ±11% of combined 1σ uncertainty, so mass spreads across all five buckets, peaking slightly in the bucket containing spot. The forecast is most sensitive to the direction of the AWS/capex surprise on Oct 29.

Amazon usually reports net sales at or slightly above the top of its guidance (about +0.4% on average over the last 9 quarters), and Q3 guidance is $197-202B. That guide is held down by Prime Day moving into Q2, while AWS is growing 37% and FX stayed close to the guide's assumption, so I centre just above the $202B consensus. The number is most sensitive to how much Prime Day timing actually removed from Q3.

Brent settled at $109.86 on 16 October and was around $108 on 19 October, with the Iran war and Hormuz disruption ongoing. I model a random walk with fat tails at about 55% annualised volatility over 8 trading days. I add a 12% chance of a US–Iran Hormuz deal, which would send the price back toward the low $90s, as after the April ceasefire. The forecast is most sensitive to whether that deal happens before 29 October.

Most crew missing after open-sea sinkings are never recovered within two weeks; HS Dignity sank and Bulgaria abandoned the search on 14 Oct, so ~52% on 0. The upside is Wine Trader, still afloat with crew likely trapped in its burned accommodation, so a batch recovery once it can be boarded is plausible; the forecast is most sensitive to whether that boarding happens before 29 Oct.

Normal October 2026 nights ran at 128-149 drones (question background), and the night of 18-19 Oct had 243 shot down (Ukrinform), so the median sits slightly above the normal cluster because the winter energy campaign is under way. The forecast is most sensitive to whether 29-30 Oct is a massive-strike night; I put about 12% on 400 or more drones, which gives a long right tail.

The Supreme Court has refused every request to stay the SIR since 2025 and upheld it in May 2026. On 15 October it only issued notice on the INDIA bloc's plea for suspension. The one hearing inside the window, on 28 October, concerns a Delhi plea for disclosure and re-inclusion, and an order there is procedural, which resolves NO. The main risk is a broad 28 October order that bars finalisation or deletions of the Delhi roll.

The repository has had one content update since launch (the 10-07 batch, merged 10-08: 6 new formalizations, bringing it to 300/719) and nothing for 11 days, so the status quo of 300 is the base case. YES needs a new batch with at least one new top-line formalization recorded in history.md by 10-29. OpenAI's public pledge to keep adding formalizations, and a possible ~3-week cadence, keep that chance material.

The count is 22 on Wikipedia today. The NHC gives disturbance EP94 a 90% chance of forming within 7 days, so Vance (the 23rd storm) is likely by Oct 29, at about 82%. Since 2014, 1-2 storms have been named in Oct 17-29 in 11 of 12 seasons, but no second area is flagged yet, so a 24th storm sits at about 26%. The forecast depends most on whether EP94 actually reaches tropical-storm strength.

Russia has rejected every limited Black Sea truce since August 2026, most recently on 2 and 9 October, and on 12 October rejected the 60-day ceasefire, insisting on a comprehensive settlement only; Kyiv will accept a maritime truce only bundled with an energy truce, and that truce collapsed within a day on 11-12 October. The one Black Sea deal that ever took effect needed about 3 months of Turkey/UN mediation, and the March 2025 US-announced deal never took effect, so a deal confirmed by both governments and in effect within 11 days is very unlikely; the main risk is a sudden US-brokered package with sanctions relief.

The official cumulative count was already 4,793 after week 41. The 1,703 the question calls cumulative is that week's figure. Three more weeks of about 1,500-2,500 closures (growth slowing, sentinel 12.81, +13%) put the cumulative total near 10,000. I keep 35% on a weekly-figure resolution near 1,900. The forecast is most sensitive to which figure the resolver uses.

In week 41 only Okinawa (31.34, falling) was at or above 30, and the next prefectures were at 20-22 (Kanagawa, Saitama, Chiba). National growth is slow (11.35 to 12.81, +13% a week), and week 42 contains a holiday. In past seasons a national average of about 15-17 has meant 0-1 prefectures at warning level. The forecast is most sensitive to whether Hokkaido (x1.76 in week 41) and Kanagawa keep accelerating.

The mayorista has stayed within 1,506-1,525 since September while the BCRA keeps buying, and it closed at 1,518 on 16 Oct (Rava, press). The forecast assumes a small upward drift (REM and year-end consensus near 1,600) and wider tails to the upside. It is most sensitive to whether the 1,505-1,530 corridor holds through 29 Oct.

No US land strike on Iran has been confirmed since about 1 September, and Israel and Iran have not exchanged fire since June. Trump has publicly pledged no attack before the 3 November midterms, and Israel says it will not act without US approval, so a deliberate campaign on 29-30 October is unlikely. The residual risk is a limited US self-defense strike after an IRGC attack on US forces, or Israeli retaliation if Iran strikes around Israel's 27 October election.

USD/KRW is at 1,331.24 on Trading Economics for Oct 19, 0.66% below the threshold. With 8 trading days of about 0.3-0.5% daily volatility, a random walk gives roughly 26-34%. The won's three-month strengthening trend pulls the number down. Policy support near 1,330 (NPS dollar buying) and a 25-33% chance of a Fed hike on Oct 28 keep upside risk alive, and that hike is the factor the forecast is most sensitive to.

The US has refused Tomahawks for Ukraine for 13 months, including when the Pentagon cleared a transfer, so the base rate for an 11-day window is about 1%. Current conditions push further toward NO: the Iran war used more than 1,000 Tomahawks and refilling the stock will take years, allied arms sales are paused, and Trump is openly hostile to Zelensky while doing deals with Putin. Only a sudden break with Moscow would change this.

ECDC's Week 42 report (data to 14 Oct) gives 19 countries, and only two more weekly reports fall before resolution. Few or no countries are usually added after mid-October, but this record 2026 season has kept adding late reporters (+3 in two weeks), so a 20th is quite possible (Türkiye, counted in 2025, is the likeliest). The forecast is most sensitive to whether any new country reports a first human case before 28 Oct.

Past US threats against Ukraine aid rarely became acknowledged pauses within 11 days, and every on-record US and NATO statement (Whitaker 13 Oct, NATO officials) calls PURL deliveries ongoing, if delayed. The risk to that view is the partial hold on PURL-funded Patriots that Hegseth has not signed (Zelensky, 18 Oct), alongside the escalating refinery-strike dispute. The forecast is most sensitive to whether a named Ukrainian official starts calling those Patriots stopped rather than not approved.

Before October, strikes off Romania ran at about one a month (about 3% a day); the October wave hit 7 ships on 5 of 16 days, but nothing has been confirmed since 15 Oct, and Romanian air defences and NATO attention are rising. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the Russian campaign against shipping anchored off Sulina resumes before 29 Oct; it rests on the blacksea.america2.news tracker and AP/Reuters-based reporting.

The question cites about 9-10 a day, but hormuz.now rebuilt its data on 19 Oct and its first full day shows 0. AIS-only series such as PortWatch (2-4 a day) and the mid-October escalation (about 20 attacks, two sinkings) support a low count. About 35% is on 0, and the forecast is most sensitive to whether the new pipeline records any crossings at all.

Formal suspension with a resumed session is rare for CBD meetings: 2 of about 17, including the most recent, COP16 in Cali. UN talks that fail usually close and defer items, which resolves NO here. A heavy finance and budget agenda and the same Friday-close calendar as Cali roughly offset the post-Cali lessons and the Rome roadmap that defers the hardest finance decisions to COP18-19. The forecast is most sensitive to whether the finance and budget texts are still bracketed going into the 30 October closing plenary.

Kaiser–CNA NorCal contracts have historically settled months after expiry, either on a strike deadline or after long drift (2015, 2018, 2022: TAs 78 or more days after expiry). As of 12 Oct 2026 the sides had held 17 sessions, wage proposals had barely been exchanged, a strike authorization vote was under way and dates were being booked through December. Only two sessions (21–22 Oct) fall before the cutoff, so a full TA by 29 Oct is very unlikely.

Anchored on the same four days in 2023: about 294k as reported live during the campaign (339k in today's table, which now includes special votes). Nudged up for the rising advance-vote share and a tight National-Labour race. The result is most sensitive to whether the 2026 daily page counts special votes and to the day-1 turnout pace.

The Ohio Supreme Court usually takes about 74 days to decide whether to hear an appeal, and the NCAA's response is not due until about early November. The court's 14 October stay is temporary, lasting only until it has considered the 19 October briefs, so its next order is most likely a ruling on the stay, which does not count. The main route to YES is a fast dismissal as moot because of DeWine's executive order, and that looks unlikely because the NCAA disputes the order in federal court.
